title: Trace elements determination in seawater by ICP-MS with on-line pre-concentration on a Chelex-100 column using a ‘standard’ instrument setup.
author: Søndergaard, Asmund, et al.
materials: The laboratory-made Chelex-100 columns were prepared by making a slurry of 1 g Chelex-100 resin (Na-form; 100–200 mesh) in 1 M NH4OH and loading it into the column using a syringe until perfectly packed. Prior to this, the resin was cleaned by soaking it in 5 M HCl overnight before it was collected on a glass microfiber filter and further cleaned with 2 M HNO3 and Milli-Q water. Glass wool was placed in the ends of the column. Before the column was used, it was conditioned with 1 M ammonium acetate buffer solution (pH 7.0) in order to convert the active sites of the resin into ammonium form and raise the pH in the column to above pH 5 [2].

A 2 M stock solution of ammonium acetate was then prepared by diluting ∼140 g of 25–35% (m/m) analytical grade ammonia hydroxide (Merck) and ∼121 g of 100% Suprapure acetic acid (Merck) in 1000 mL of Milli-Q water. The pH was adjusted to 7.0 by adding either ammonia hydroxide or acetic acid. Last, the ammonium acetate buffer solution was purified by passing it through a 100 mm Chelex-100 filled glass column. From the purified stock buffer solution a 0.05 M ammonium acetate buffer solution was prepared by diluting the stock solution 1:40 with Milli-Q water. All Milli-Q water (18 MΩ cm−1) was purified in a Milli-Q water purification system (Millipore, Bedford, MA).
Finally, the standards as well as the samples (pH ∼1.
were diluted 1:1 with the purified 2 M ammonium acetate buffer solution (pH 7.
resulting in a final pH of 6.1–6.
Polyethylene vials were used for standards and samples and were thoroughly cleaned with 10% nitric acid and Milli-Q water prior to use.

steps.title: Prepare Chelex‑100 column
steps.instruction: Clean, pack, and condition a laboratory‑made Chelex‑100 column for on‑line pre‑concentration.

substeps.instruction: Soak 1 g Chelex‑100 resin (Na‑form; 100–200 mesh) in 5 M HCl overnight.
Collect the resin on a glass microfiber filter and rinse sequentially with 2 M HNO₃ and Milli‑Q water.
Make a slurry of the cleaned resin in 1 M NH₄OH.
Load the slurry into a column using a syringe until the resin is perfectly packed; place glass wool at both ends of the column.
Condition the packed column with 1 M ammonium acetate buffer (pH 7.0) to convert the active sites to the ammonium form and raise the column pH above 5.

steps.title: Prepare 2 M ammonium acetate stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a 2 M ammonium acetate buffer solution and purify it.

substeps.instruction: Weigh approximately 140 g of 25–35 % (m/m) analytical‑grade ammonia hydroxide (Merck) and 121 g of 100 % Suprapure acetic acid (Merck).
Dilute both reagents in 1000 mL Milli‑Q water (18 MΩ cm⁻¹) to obtain a 2 M ammonium acetate solution.
Adjust the pH to 7.0 by adding either ammonia hydroxide or acetic acid as needed.
Pass the prepared stock buffer through a 100 mm Chelex‑100‑filled glass column to purify it.

steps.title: Prepare 0.05 M buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute the purified 2 M ammonium acetate stock to obtain a 0.05 M buffer.

substeps.instruction: Mix the purified 2 M stock with Milli‑Q water at a 1:40 ratio (1 part stock + 39 parts water).

steps.title: Prepare and dilute standards
steps.instruction: Create calibration standards using CRM NASS‑5 and dilute them with buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add Agilent multi‑element calibration standard‑2A to certified seawater reference material (CRM) NASS‑5 to achieve final concentrations of 0, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, and 10 µg L⁻¹ for V, Mn, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, As, Cd, and Pb above the concentrations already present in NASS‑5.
Dilute each standard 1:1 with the purified 2 M ammonium acetate buffer (pH 7.0); the resulting mixture has a final pH of 6.1–6.3.
Prepare samples (initial pH ≈ 1.6) in the same way: 1:1 dilution with the purified 2 M buffer.
Use polyethylene vials for all standards and samples; clean vials thoroughly with 10 % nitric acid followed by Milli‑Q water before use.

steps.title: Measure elution peaks and column efficiency
steps.instruction: Run the ICP‑MS method, record time‑series elution peaks, and evaluate column performance.

substeps.instruction: Inject each diluted sample and standard onto the Chelex‑100 column and record the elution peak for each trace element.

Calculate column efficiency by comparing the amount of each element that entered the column during pre‑concentration to the total amount eluted, using the integrated area of the elution peak versus the signal from a 100 µg L⁻¹ solution run without the column.
Correct all analyte signals with the internal standards Ge, Rh, and Ir.

steps.title: Determine concentrations and calibrate
steps.instruction: Process peak data to obtain sample concentrations and construct calibration curves.

substeps.instruction: For each elution peak, determine the average peak count over an ~175 s interval (25 replicate measurements).
Obtain the average signal directly from Agilent’s Fileview software; no additional software is required.
Correct the average peak counts for variations in the internal standards.
Construct calibration curves from the corrected peak counts of the standards; no blank corrections are applied.
Assess method accuracy by measuring the certified reference materials SLEW‑3 and CASS‑4.
